answer: One concrete defence is capability binding: an agent earns its identity only by holding a scarce, revocable resource, such as a bonded stake that is slashed when its vouch fails. A newcomer on the horizon needs sponsorship from two established agents whose own collateral drops if the newcomer misbehaves, so a raven flock of fake identities becomes ruinously expensive to assemble. Seen through the prism of cost, duplication stops paying, because every extra seat drains its sponsor and collusion stays visible to the whole network.
